name: Imatinib (Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasm with Eosinophilia, PDGFRA- or PDGFRB-rearranged)
disease: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusion (MLNe)
histology: myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia harboring a PDGFRA (eg FIP1L1::PDGFRA) or PDGFRB rearrangement; may present in chronic phase or as blast phase (AML, ALL, mixed-phenotype acute leukemia, or extramedullary myeloid sarcoma / lymphoblastic lymphoma)

biomarkers.PDGFRA: rearrangement (eg FIP1L1::PDGFRA) - dramatically imatinib-sensitive; this is the biomarker gate for imatinib
biomarkers.PDGFRB: rearrangement - imatinib-sensitive; this is the biomarker gate for imatinib
biomarkers.FGFR1: rearrangement is NOT imatinib-responsive (treated with an FGFR1-active agent eg pemigatinib or midostaurin, per MLNE-7) - do not use imatinib
biomarkers.JAK2: rearrangement is NOT imatinib-responsive (treated with a JAK2-active agent eg ruxolitinib, per MLNE-8) - do not use imatinib
biomarkers.resistanceMutations: PDGFRA T674I and D842V are imatinib-resistant kinase-domain mutations (false-negative guard: a PDGFRA-rearranged case that fails imatinib should be evaluated for these)
biomarkers.note: Imatinib is the recommended first-line tyrosine kinase inhibitor ONLY for MLNe driven by a PDGFRA or PDGFRB rearrangement. FGFR1- and JAK2-rearranged MLNe are NOT imatinib-responsive and are directed to other targeted agents (pemigatinib/midostaurin for FGFR1; ruxolitinib for JAK2). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions, MLNE-5 (PDGFRA), MLNE-6 (PDGFRB), MLNE-7 (FGFR1), MLNE-8 (JAK2), and DeVita 12th ed. / Harrison 22nd ed.

treatmentSetting: chronic phase (also used in blast phase, with or as an adjunct to acute-leukemia induction chemotherapy)
lineOfTherapy: first-line for PDGFRA- or PDGFRB-rearranged MLNe (induction and maintenance); durable complete hematologic and cytogenetic (FISH) responses are achieved in the vast majority

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: PDGFRA rearrangement (eg FIP1L1::PDGFRA, cytogenetically occult - requires FISH for CHIC2 deletion) or PDGFRB rearrangement
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, MLNE-5 (PDGFRA: Imatinib 100 mg daily) and MLNE-6 (PDGFRB: Imatinib 100-400 mg daily, 400 mg generally used as induction)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: in patients with symptoms/signs of cardiac involvement (troponinemia and/or abnormal ECHO), give concurrent corticosteroids for 7 to 10 days when starting imatinib and obtain cardiology consultation (eosinophil-mediated cardiac damage risk)
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, MLNE-5 / MLNE-6 (concurrent corticosteroids for 7-10 days in patients with signs of cardiac involvement); mlne lines 470, 529

exclusionCriteria.requirement: FGFR1 rearrangement (not imatinib-responsive; directed to pemigatinib or an FGFR1-active TKI per MLNE-7)
exclusionCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions
exclusionCriteria.locator: v2.2026, MLNE-7 (Pemigatinib; TKI with activity against FGFR1 eg midostaurin); mlne lines 588, 629

exclusionCriteria.requirement: JAK2 rearrangement (not imatinib-responsive; directed to ruxolitinib per MLNE-8)
exclusionCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions
exclusionCriteria.locator: v2.2026, MLNE-8 (TKI with activity against JAK2: Ruxolitinib); mlne lines 645, 664

exclusionCriteria.requirement: PDGFRA T674I or D842V kinase-domain mutation (imatinib-resistant; consider clinical trial of an active TKI eg avapritinib for D842V)
exclusionCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions
exclusionCriteria.locator: v2.2026, MLNE-5 footnote u (PDGFRA T674I and D842V mutations are resistant to imatinib) footnote v (avapritinib); DeVita 12th ed. line 22631

drugs.name: Imatinib

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloid/Lymphoid Neoplasms with Eosinophilia and Tyrosine Kinase Gene Fusions
provenance.locator: MLNE-5 (PDGFRA rearrangement: Imatinib 100 mg daily; footnote t maintenance as low as 100-200 mg weekly after sustained CHR/CCyR); MLNE-6 (PDGFRB rearrangement: Imatinib 100-400 mg daily, 400 mg generally used as induction); mlne lines 470, 474, 485, 529, 546, 574, 1758-1772

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) MLNe v2.2026, MLNE-5 and MLNE-6; DeVita 12th ed. (FIP1L1-PDGFRA imatinib, line 22660) and Harrison 22nd ed. (line 124607, excellent response to imatinib). Imatinib is given continuously PO once daily (represented as days 1 to 28). DOSE VARIES BY FUSION: PDGFRA-rearranged (eg FIP1L1::PDGFRA) - 100 mg daily (modeled value); PDGFRB-rearranged - 100 to 400 mg daily, with 400 mg daily generally used as the induction dose (MLNE-6); blast-phase disease - 100 to 400 mg daily, may be added to AML- or ALL-type induction chemotherapy or given as monotherapy (MLNE-5/MLNE-6). MAINTENANCE: after sustained complete hematologic and complete cytogenetic (FISH) response, doses as low as 100-200 mg weekly have been used (MLNE-5 footnote t); reduction to 100 mg daily may be considered for PDGFRB after CHR/CCyR (MLNE-6 footnote x). No ISMP tall-man form for imatinib.

supportiveCare: Concurrent corticosteroids for 7 to 10 days when initiating imatinib in patients with symptoms/signs of cardiac involvement (troponinemia and/or abnormal ECHO); cardiology consultation recommended (eosinophil-mediated cardiac damage / heart failure risk). Source: NCCN MLNe v2.2026, MLNE-5/MLNE-6.

Continuous daily oral dosing with no defined cycle count; continue for durable response and monitor for cytogenetic/molecular clonal evolution (including imatinib-resistance mutations PDGFRA T674I/D842V).
Tumor lysis / high eosinophil-burden precautions and cardiac monitoring at initiation given the eosinophilic disease context.

monitoring: CBC and absolute eosinophil count (hematologic response; CHR typically by 1 month)
cytogenetic response by FISH (typically by 3 months) and, if available, molecular response by RT-PCR, every 3 to 6 months
cardiac assessment (troponin, ECHO) at initiation for eosinophil-mediated cardiac injury
imaging to document target-organ / extramedullary disease response if clinically indicated
evaluate adherence and screen for resistance mutations (PDGFRA T674I/D842V) on loss of response

doseModificationRules.text: Imatinib 100 to 400 mg daily, with 400 mg daily generally used as the induction dose (NCCN MLNe v2.2026, MLNE-6; mlne lines 529, 546).
Imatinib 100 to 400 mg daily; may be added to AML- or ALL-type induction chemotherapy or given as monotherapy (NCCN MLNe v2.2026, MLNE-5/MLNE-6; mlne lines 485, 546).
Maintenance doses as low as 100-200 mg weekly have been used with sustained responses (MLNE-5 footnote t); reduction to 100 mg daily may be considered for PDGFRB after CHR/CCyR (MLNE-6 footnote x).

Evaluate adherence and for clonal evolution / imatinib-resistance mutations (PDGFRA T674I, D842V); if a resistance mutation is found consider a TKI with potential activity (eg avapritinib for D842V) or refer for clinical trial, and consider HCT evaluation. Obtain clinical review.

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for imatinib in PDGFRA- or PDGFRB-rearranged myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia (MLNe), a rare myeloid disorder. Imatinib doses are dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) MLNe v2.2026: 100 mg daily for PDGFRA rearrangement (MLNE-5) and 100-400 mg daily (400 mg generally used as induction) for PDGFRB rearrangement (MLNE-6), with maintenance as low as 100-200 mg weekly (MLNE-5 footnote t); the core framework is DeVita 12th ed. (line 22660) and Harrison 22nd ed. (line 124607). The modeled starting value is the PDGFRA 100 mg dose; PDGFRB 400 mg, blast-phase 100-400 mg, and maintenance de-escalation are carried as dose-modification rules and notes rather than separate protocols, and no dose is invented (no field is VERIFY). BIOMARKER GATE: imatinib is used only for PDGFRA/PDGFRB rearrangement; FGFR1 rearrangement (MLNE-7, pemigatinib/midostaurin) and JAK2 rearrangement (MLNE-8, ruxolitinib) are explicitly NOT imatinib-responsive and are captured as exclusions, as are the imatinib-resistant PDGFRA T674I/D842V mutations (DeVita line 22631). This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
